Variants.Content: Stonehall is an important market town in the Riverlands, located in the area where the King's Road meets many local roads. It was named for its stone church, and its inn, blacksmith shop, market and stables made it a natural stopping point for travelers. Dynastic wars and noble rebellions passed through the town many times, making Stonehall appear more often in the history books than many castles; but for its residents, the real history is the weekly markets, tax days, services, weddings and crops ripening. It has no dangerous mountain passes to rely on, nor dangerous rivers, so convenient transportation always coexists with exposure.

Entry Stony Sept Local families also relied on river transportation, ferries, wheat fields, mills, and hiding places when war came; if any road, well, spring, or dock failed, the price would fall first on them.

Entry Stony Sept If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

Stone and wood will decay, but Shitang Town still relies on craftsmen to take care of quarrying stone, logging, iron parts, goat hair, and building wall foundations close to the mountain. It relies on priests to preserve the memory of the Seven Gods, the legend of the ancient river king, and the land that changed hands repeatedly. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Stony Sept They care about river transportation, ferries, wheat fields, mills, and hiding places when war comes. They also care about whether seeds are left after collecting grain and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
